subject.title: Exploring a chat-first Android surface for OpenClaw (discussion + possible focused upstreaming)

question: Should the official Android app move toward a chat-first default/mode, accept focused UX/media slices while keeping the current companion-node shape, or leave chat-first forks outside core for now?
rationale: Current main partially addresses Android chat access, but changing launch defaults or broader media/connectivity behavior affects onboarding, gateway pairing, permissions, security, and release posture.

options.title: Scope focused Android slices
options.body: Keep this issue open while Android owners define narrow launch/navigation, media, and connectivity PR slices with real-device proof.

options.title: Keep companion-first Android
options.body: Document that official Android remains a gateway companion surface and ask chat-first fork authors to file only specific defects or narrow UX improvements.

options.title: Sponsor chat-first mode
options.body: Explicitly approve a chat-first default or mode and require upgrade, onboarding, media-permission, and real-device proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Scope focused Android slices
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while Android owners define narrow launch/navigation, media, and connectivity PR slices with real-device proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The Android app ownership docs and history route this product-surface decision to @obviyus.
